transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-19
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions Eng), Alex Ramirez (CTO, Starlite), Priya Shah (Head of Cloud, Starlite), Jared Cole (Biz Dev, Starlite)

[00:00] Ethan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick round of intros and then we'll go through what Starlite is seeing in the market and where Redwood might fit.
[00:18] Alex (Starlite): Yeah hi, Alex here. Starlite does managed integrations for enterprises  mostly telco and finance  we resell cloud and bundle infra + ops. We're exploring partnerships for inference stack, especially for customers asking about private deployments and compliance.
[00:36] Priya (Starlite): Priya here. We run multi-cloud fleets, mix of Nvidia A100s and some H100s in newer clusters, and also do on-prem installs. Main asks: can you support a private on-prem workflow, what security controls, and how would pricing / reseller margins look.
[00:53] Maya (SE): Thanks. Quick high level on Redwood: we offer hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity and Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments. The runtime has batching, KV cache and quantization optimizations  sorry, K-V cash in speech to text sometimes. We also provide rollouts, canaries, and observability.
[01:15] Jordan (Solutions Eng): For partners you might be both a reseller and an SI  typical flow is pilot on Dedicated for predictable perf, then option to convert to Private for customers needing air-gapped.
[01:32] Alex: Makes sense. For Starlite, our ops teams care about network setup  VPC peering, private link, and customer KMS. Do you support HSM integrations?
[01:45] Maya: Yes we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; in Private deployments the customer controls keys. We can do SSO/SAML, RBAC, and we produce audit logs for requests. We also have SOC 2 reports. (some words overlapped)
[02:05] Ethan: From a GTM lens we typically do revenue-share or referral depending on contract size. Starlite as a managed services partner could either resell Dedicated capacity or onboard customers to Private with our enterprise licensing.
[02:23] Priya: On the security pack  can you share SOC 2 and pen test summaries? Also log retention policies; one customer requires 7 years.
[02:36] Maya: We'll send the security pack. Retention is configurable depending on plan; for Private it's customer controlled. For hosted we have retention defaults but enterprise add-ons allow longer retention.
[02:50] Alex: On pilot mechanics  we want to run benchmark tests: throughput with batching, p99 latency on typical prompt lengths (they mentioned 128/512 tokens), and cost per token estimates. Can Redwood provide a perf harness?
[03:08] Jordan: Yes, SE can run the perf harness. We'll want sample prompts and an eval set from you  ideally representative of your customers (LLM routing, multi-turn chat). We support continuous batching and prefix caching which affects throughput.
[03:28] Alex: Any rough numbers for H100 vs A100? Our ops team defaults to A100 but many customers want H100 for cost-efficiency with certain quantization.
[03:40] Maya: H100 tends to be better for larger models but depends on quantization; we'll show model-specific profiles. Also note kernel selection in the runtime optimizes based on sequence lengths. We'll capture those in the benchmark report.
[03:57] Priya: Network egress is a blocker for some customers  if we're reselling cloud capacity, what are the routing options? Can we keep traffic inside a customer's VPC?
[04:10] Maya: For Private we deploy into customer VPC or on-prem; for Dedicated we can set up VPC peering and private link. We also support regional routing to keep data in specific geos for residency.
[04:26] Ethan: Curious about partner enablement  training, co-marketing, sales engineering hours, and the partner portal. Starlite: how do you normally structure reseller agreements?
[04:38] Jared (Starlite): We usually want tiered margins based on committed spend, and some co-selling credits for the first six months. Also a technical onboarding allowance.
[04:48] Ethan: That aligns with common Redwood partner deals  we can put together a starter template with tiers for Dedicated commits and Private licensing. We'll propose a partner discount and a referral vs reseller flow.
[05:02] Alex: From a technical perspective, what are integration touchpoints? API keys, IAM roles, telemetry hooks for billing visibility, and alerting for SLA breaches.
[05:14] Maya: API keys + token-based auth for hosted. For Dedicated/Private we support IAM role mapping and can push metrics into your Prometheus/Grafana; also token-level cost breakdown in the Console. We provide tracing hooks and exportable logs for audit.
[05:34] Alex: Any gotchas with on-prem? Like GPU driver versions or custom kernels?
[05:41] Maya: Drivers matter  we publish supported stacks (CUDA versions, drivers). On-prem can be trickier with older GPUs; we have an on-prem package and recommended hardware profiles. We also have optional optimization for quantized runtimes which may need specific kernels.
[05:58] Priya: For large enterprise customers, legal often asks for indemnity and data processing addendum. Do you have standard templates?
[06:07] Ethan: Yes, we have DPA and standard EULA templates. For enterprise deals we can negotiate terms; we'll also provide SOC2 and relevant compliance docs.
[06:20] Alex: Could you walk through a hypothetical pilot? Steps and timeline?
[06:26] Jordan: Typical pilot: 1) discovery + scoping (this call), 2) technical deep-dive with infra teams to collect diagrams and traffic flows, 3) pilot cluster provisioning (Dedicated or Private) and perf tests (1-2 weeks), 4) evaluation and decision. Total ~3-6 weeks depending on procurement.
[06:46] Alex: That's acceptable. For procurement, some customers need an invoice + PO process; Redwood support that?
[06:52] Ethan: Yes, enterprise invoicing and PO is supported. We also have marketplace options for certain cloud providers.
[07:02] Priya: On models  do you support bringing customer models or only hosted catalog? Customers sometimes want to bring bespoke LLMs.
[07:10] Maya: We support customer model onboarding for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we provide curated open models and verified performance. We also support model pinning and versioning for rollouts.
[07:22] Alex: For managed services we might want to offer a bundled support SLA  can Redwood provide white-label or co-managed options?
[07:30] Ethan: We have partner programs that allow co-managed operations; we'll detail support tiers in the partner pack.
[07:38] Jared: On pricing transparency  can the Console show token-level cost split so we can bill customers?
[07:45] Jordan: Yes Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model, and you can export the reports for billing.
[07:54] Priya: About security scanning  do you run regular pen tests? Any bug bounty?
[07:59] Maya: We do internal and third-party pen tests; details in the security pack. We also integrate with customer SIEMs for alerting.
[08:08] Alex: Great. Any reference customers in regulated industries?
[08:12] Ethan: We have finance and healthcare customers on Dedicated and Private  we'll try to include anonymized references in the partner doc.
[08:20] Alex: On the tech deep-dive for the pilot, who should join from our side? Probably Priya + infra eng.
[08:26] Jordan: Yes, and whoever manages GPU ops and security. We'll propose times.
[08:32] Ethan: Let's talk about logs and data retention again  some of our customers need 7 years, others require encryption-at-rest and customer-managed keys. Does Redwood allow that for Private?
[08:44] Maya: Customer-managed keys: yes. Long-term retention for hosted can be accommodated with add-on. For Private it's in your control.
[08:51] Alex: Okay. Ongoings: co-marketing. Starlite would like to do a joint webinar once we have a pilot success story. What does Redwood typically require?
[08:59] Ethan: A short case study, 2-3 page joint deck, and a 30-45 min webinar. We'll support with SDRs and campaign assets.
[09:08] Jared: Sounds good. A couple of quick technical clarifications: 1) latency SLOs under network constraints; 2) model fallback options.
[09:17] Maya: We support smart routing and fallbacks  e.g., route to a smaller model variant or hosted fallback if Dedicated under capacity. For latency SLOs we expose p99 metrics and can set alerts.
[09:30] Priya: For the perf harness, what sample size do you run? We need statistically significant runs.
[09:36] Jordan: We'll run multiple trials per prompt length and provide aggregated p50/p95/p99 plus throughput. We'll also show the effect of batching and prefix caching.
[09:48] Alex: Any pre-reqs from our side to run the benchmark?
[09:51] Maya: Access to sample prompt set, target model, and network details. If it's Private or Dedicated we'll need access to the cluster or temporary accounts.
[10:02] Ethan: To keep momentum, we'll follow up with the partner playbook and propose times for the deep-dive.
[10:08] Alex: Quick note: some customers use a mix of Nvidia and AMD GPUs  do you support AMD?
[10:14] Maya: We have limited support for AMD; main optimization path is Nvidia (A100/H100). On-prem AMD can be supported case-by-case.
[10:23] Priya: Also curious about model quantization support  we see customers want int8 + 4-bit quantization for cost savings.
[10:30] Maya: We support quantization-friendly execution paths; the runtime picks kernels accordingly. Quantized throughput and quality tradeoffs will be in the benchmark.
[10:40] Alex: Anything else on licensing? Some customers want perpetual on-prem license.
[10:44] Ethan: For private deployments we offer licensing + support; perpetual can be discussed with legal.
[10:49] Jordan: For the technical deep-dive we can demo Dedicated performance on a small cluster and share the perf spreadsheet. We'll pre-populate with example numbers.
[10:58] Priya: OK thanks. One more: compliance in EMEA  data residency and DPA are must-haves.
[11:05] Maya: We can deploy in customer regions and sign DPAs that reflect EU requirements. We'll annotate the security pack with regional notes.
[11:15] Alex: Great. Let's capture action items.
[11:19] Ethan: I'll send the partner pack and partner pricing template. Maya will set up the technical deep-dive. Priya / Alex will share infra diagrams and GPU inventory. Jared will share GTM contacts.
[11:32] Alex: Thanks all. Good first call.
[11:35] Ethan: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

(Transcript ends  occasional word swaps and minor mis-attributions from auto-transcription.)
